# Requirements Document: Declining an airline change

## Introduction

A customer who does not want a change the airline made can answer it with the
Cancel or Reshop follow-up action.  The airline prices the answer as it prices
any cancellation or change, with a price differential.  The sources never say
whether the airline's cancellation and change fees apply when the customer
declines a change the airline imposed, and no source defines which changes
the airline imposes.  The model takes both answers as parameters, readings of
the sources.

These requirements are generated from the Lean model in [`Rules/OneOrder/AirlineChange/Decline.lean`](https://github.com/samdengler/verified-air/blob/main/Rules/OneOrder/AirlineChange/Decline.lean). Each acceptance criterion carries the status the build computed for it: *proven* means a theorem the build checked, *example only* means a computed example, *open* means a theorem the build could not prove, and *not checked* means no theorem or example covers it yet.

## Requirements

### Requirement ONE-703

**User Story:** As a customer, I want to know what declining a change the airline made will cost me, so that I can choose between the changed trip, another trip and my money back.

**Rule:** WHEN a customer declines an airline change through Cancel or Reshop THE SYSTEM SHALL price it as a cancellation or change of the affected order items, with the airline's cancellation or change fee as the penalty. (Lean: `declineOffer`)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a customer declines an airline change through Cancel or Auto-cancellation THE SYSTEM SHALL price a cancellation of the affected order items with a new price of zero.
   - ONE-703.1, proven: proven theorem `decline_cancel_prices`; example `autoCancellation`; example `carrierChangeDeclined`; example `declineByCancel`
2. WHEN a customer declines an airline change through Reshop THE SYSTEM SHALL price a change from the affected order items to the new items at their price.
   - ONE-703.2, proven: proven theorem `decline_reshop_prices`; example `declineByReshop`
3. IF a customer declines an involuntary change through Cancel or Auto-cancellation THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL charge no cancellation penalty.
   - ONE-703.4, open: open theorem `decline_cancel_no_penalty`; counterexample `autoCancellation`; counterexample `declineByCancel`
4. IF a customer declines an involuntary change through Reshop THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL charge no change fee.
   - ONE-703.5, open: open theorem `decline_reshop_no_fee`; counterexample `declineByReshop`

#### Open question on ONE-703.4

> A customer who declines an involuntary change through Cancel, or whose
> seller lets it lapse into Auto-cancellation, pays no cancellation penalty.
>
> Open question for the business.  The sources offer Cancel as an answer to an
> airline change and never say whether the airline's fees apply; the
> cancellation page leaves penalties to the airline.  Under the reading that
> applies the item's fees, the 50 EUR cancellation fee of the itinerary change
> worked example is charged for leaving a change the airline made.  The example
> `declineByCancel` shows it.  Do the airline's cancellation fees apply
> when the customer declines a change the airline imposed?

#### Open question on ONE-703.5

> A customer who declines an involuntary change through Reshop pays no change
> fee.
>
> Open question for the business.  The sources say a reshop after an airline
> change may or may not cost the customer more, and give no rule.  Under the
> reading that applies the item's fees, the 40 EUR change fee of the itinerary
> change worked example is charged when the customer reshops away from flights
> the airline moved.  The example `declineByReshop` shows it.  Do change
> fees and fare differences apply when the customer reshops after an airline
> change, and which alternatives must the airline offer?
